# MODULE 1: Payroll Run Engine

**Path:** `modules/payroll-run/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/payroll-run/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

The Payroll Run Engine is the heart of the entire system. It is a multi-step processing wizard that gathers data from every other module — attendance records, wage profiles, government benefits, loans, allowances, and manual adjustments — and calculates each employee's gross pay, deductions, and final net pay.

The engine flows through four defined stages:
- **Stage 1 — Configure**: HR selects the cutoff period and department, then enters a security password.
- **Stage 2 — Adjust**: The system aggregates all data (a "workspace") and computes a draft pay register. HR can flag employees as "on hold" or add manual line items.
- **Stage 3 — Process**: The computed register is saved to the database as a `DRAFT` record.
- **Stage 4 — Review & Post**: HR finalises and posts the payroll, locking all records permanently.

---

### 2. FILES & FUNCTIONS

#### `providers/payrollRunService.ts`
The primary business logic service. Largest file in the project (~3,000 lines).

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| `isActiveByDeletedFlags(args)` | Checks whether an employee and their wage record are active (not soft-deleted). Used to filter out terminated employees before computation. |
| `listCutoffs()` | Fetches all available cutoff period settings from `cutoff_settings`, sorted by newest first. |
| `listDepartments()` | Fetches all departments from the `department` table, sorted alphabetically by name. |
| `findExistingPostedRun(args)` | Searches `payroll_run` for an already-POSTED run that matches the given cutoff ID and department. |
| `findExistingDraftRun(args)` | Searches `payroll_run` for an existing DRAFT or PROCESSED (not yet posted) run for the same cutoff and department. |
| `generatePayrollRefNo(args)` | Builds a short, unique reference string for the payroll run (e.g. `PR-5-20260701-20260715`). |
| `createOrGetActiveRun(args)` | Idempotent "get or create" function. Returns the existing DRAFT run if one exists; otherwise creates a new one in the database. Handles race conditions using unique constraint retries. |
| `createDraftRun(args)` | Creates a brand-new DRAFT payroll run. Blocks creation if a POSTED run with no on-hold employees already exists for the same period. |
| `loadWorkspace(args)` | **Core data aggregation function.** Fetches all employees, wages, attendance, holidays, proration logs, manual additions/deductions, DR payments, retro pay, allowances, benefit settings, employee loans, benefit loans, and coop savings for the selected cutoff period — all in one batch. |
| `loadPersistedHoldMap(payrollRunId)` | Loads the set of employees currently marked `on_hold = 1` for a given run from `payroll_run_employee`. |
| `loadPostedEmployeesMap(payrollRunId)` | Loads employees whose lines have been fully posted (to prevent reprocessing). |
| `enforceOnHoldEmployeesAndMaybeRerun(args)` | After a partial posting, checks if held employees remain and triggers a re-computation for them. |
| `computeRegister(args)` | Loops over all employees in the workspace and calls `computeEmployeeLine()` for each one, assembling the full payroll register. |
| `isEmployeeOnHold(user)` | Returns `true` if the user is flagged as on-hold in the current run. |
| `isLineOnHold(line, holdMap)` | Checks a computed payroll line against the hold map to determine if it should be excluded from posting totals. |
| `filterPayslipLines(lines, holdMap)` | Filters computed lines to exclude on-hold employees, producing the final payslip-eligible list. |
| `createManualEntry(args)` | Inserts a new manual addition or deduction line item into `payroll_other_additions` or `payroll_other_deductions`. |
| `updateManualEntry(args)` | Updates an existing manual entry. |
| `deleteManualEntry(args)` | Deletes a manual entry. |
| `createDRPaymentDeduction(args)` | Creates a `dr_payment` record flagged as a payroll deduction for the current cutoff period. |
| `updateDRPayment(args)` | Updates a DR payment record's amount or details. |
| `deleteDRPayment(args)` | Deletes a DR payment record. |
| `updateDRPaymentDeduction(args)` | Updates the amount of an existing DR payment deduction. |
| `deleteDRPaymentDeduction(args)` | Removes a DR payment deduction entry. |
| `saveLines(args)` | **Bulk saves** all computed `payroll_run_employee` rows and `payroll_run_employee_item` line items to the database. Also updates the run header totals (headcount, gross, deductions, net). |
| `postRun(args)` | **Finalises the payroll.** Changes `payroll_run.status` from `PROCESSED` to `POSTED`. Records all posted source deductions in `payroll_source_posting` to prevent double-deduction. Marks DR payments as posted. |
| `updateRunTotals(args)` | Recalculates and patches the `payroll_run` header's `total_gross`, `total_deductions`, `total_net`, `headcount`, and `variance_alert_count` aggregates. |

#### `utils/compute.ts`
The pure calculation engine. Contains no API calls — only mathematical logic.

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| `parseCutoffValue(value)` | Parses a cutoff string in `"YYYY-MM-DD_YYYY-MM-DD"` format into `{ start, end }` objects. |
| `formatPHP(amount)` | Formats a number into Philippine Peso currency string (e.g. `₱1,250.00`). |
| `buildManualItemizationsForBreakdown(manualEntries)` | Converts raw manual entries into formatted breakdown items for payslip display. |
| `buildEmployeeLoanItemsForBreakdown(employeeLoans)` | Converts employee loan records into formatted deduction breakdown items. |
| `computeEmployeeLine(args)` | **The core computation function.** Given all workspace inputs for one employee, calculates: daily rate, proration split, basic pay, overtime pay, holiday pay (with multipliers), rest day pay, night differential, allowances, retro pay, government contribution deductions, loan deductions, benefit loan deductions, coop savings deductions, DR deductions, and net pay. |

**Holiday Multiplier Logic (inside `computeEmployeeLine`):**

| Scenario | Base Multiplier | OT Multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| Regular Holiday only | 2.00× | 2.60× |
| Special Holiday / Sunday only | 1.30× | 1.69× |
| Special + Rest Day | 1.50× | 1.95× |
| Regular + Rest Day | 2.60× | 3.38× |
| Night Differential | +10% on hourly rate | — |

#### `providers/payrollAdjustmentsService.ts`
Handles CRUD operations for manual adjustments within the Adjust step.

#### `providers/payrollApi.ts`
Low-level HTTP client functions (`listItems`, `createItem`, `patchItem`, `getItem`, `deleteItem`) that proxy requests to the Directus backend.

#### `providers/payslipPdfService.ts`
Generates PDF payslips using the computed `payroll_run_employee` data.

#### `utils/payslipPdf.ts`
PDF layout and rendering logic for individual employee payslips.

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- payroll_run: Header record for each payroll processing session
CREATE TABLE `payroll_run` (
  `payroll_run_id` BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `cutoff_id`      BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,          -- FK to cutoff_settings
  `cutoff_type`    ENUM('FIRST','SECOND') NULL,
  `cutoff_start`   DATE NOT NULL,
  `cutoff_end`     DATE NOT NULL,
  `department_id`  INT NULL DEFAULT NULL,              -- NULL = all departments
  `status`         ENUM('DRAFT','PROCESSED','POSTED','VOID') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'DRAFT',
  `payroll_ref_no` VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,               -- unique reference e.g. PR-5-20260701-20260715
  `headcount`      INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `total_gross`    DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `total_deductions` DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `total_net`      DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `variance_alert_count` INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `remarks`        VARCHAR(255) NULL DEFAULT NULL,
  `created_by`     INT NOT NULL,
  `created_at`     DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `processed_at`   DATETIME NULL DEFAULT NULL,
  `posted_by`      INT NULL DEFAULT NULL,
  `posted_at`      DATETIME NULL DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`payroll_run_id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_payroll_ref_no` (`payroll_ref_no`) USING BTREE,
  INDEX `idx_payroll_run_cutoff_dept` (`cutoff_id`, `department_id`, `status`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- payroll_source_posting: Prevents the same source record (e.g. a DR payment) from being deducted twice
CREATE TABLE `payroll_source_posting` (
  `id`            BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `payroll_run_id` BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `source_table`  VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,                -- e.g. 'dr_payment'
  `source_pk`     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,                -- PK of the deducted source record
  `employee_id`   INT NOT NULL,
  `amount`        DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `created_at`    DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_source_once` (`source_table`, `source_pk`) USING BTREE -- prevents re-deduction
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

### 4. REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS

**Scenario A — Standard First-Cutoff Payroll**

> Event 1: HR opens the payroll wizard and selects "July 2026 — 1st Cutoff" and "Logistics Department."
> Event 2: `loadWorkspace()` runs, fetching all employees, their wages, approved attendance for July 1–15, holidays, proration logs, and any active loans, allowances, or DR deductions.
> Event 3: `computeRegister()` calls `computeEmployeeLine()` per employee. An employee with approved 480 work minutes on a Regular Holiday (e.g. June 12) gets base pay × 2.0 multiplier plus 2.6× for any overtime minutes.
> Event 4: Computed lines are stored in `payroll_run` (status=`DRAFT`) and `payroll_run_employee`.
> Event 5: HR reviews the register, flags one new-hire as "On Hold," and clicks "Post."
> Event 6: `postRun()` changes status to `POSTED`, writes all DR deductions to `payroll_source_posting`, and queues payslips in `payroll_payslip` (status=`PENDING`).

**Scenario B — Salary Increase Mid-Cutoff (Proration)**

> Event 1: HR updated an employee's daily wage from ₱750 to ₱850 effective July 10. This created a `user_wage_proration_log` record.
> Event 2: `loadWorkspace()` loads the proration log alongside the active wage.
> Event 3: `computeEmployeeLine()` detects the proration log and switches to a "DailyRateResolver" — July 1–9 at ₱750/day, July 10–15 at ₱850/day.
> Event 4: The resulting `payroll_run_employee.proration_json` stores a day-by-day breakdown for payslip transparency.

---

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **Never delete a POSTED run.** Instead, void it using the `VOID` status. Deleting rows from `payroll_run_employee` while a run is POSTED will break the `payroll_source_posting` integrity checks.
- **`uq_source_once` is critical.** The unique index on `payroll_source_posting (source_table, source_pk)` is your only guard against double-deduction of DR payments. Do not drop this constraint.
- **On-hold re-run logic.** A POSTED run can be re-entered for on-hold employees only. `createOrGetActiveRun()` checks for on-hold employees before allowing re-run creation.

# MODULE 2: Wage Management

**Path:** `modules/wage/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/wage/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

The Wage Management module is the secure master record editor for employee salary data. It stores daily rates, government contribution amounts (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG), leave entitlements, and flags like `isCard` (salary via ATM card) and `isRegularEmployee`. Because compensation data is sensitive, the module requires a secondary password verification step before any employee's data can be viewed or modified — every access attempt is logged.

The module is also the central hub where HR manages all per-employee financial adjustments — employee loans, retro pay, allowances, other additions/deductions, DR payments, coop savings memberships, benefit loans, and benefit logs — all scoped to a specific employee selected from the paginated employee list.

---

| `patchCoopSavingsMembership(id, payload)` | `coop_savings_membership` | Updates a coop savings membership. |
| `deleteCoopSavingsMembership(id)` | `coop_savings_membership` | Removes a coop savings membership. |
| `fetchBenefitLogsByUser(userId)` | `benefit_logs` | Fetches the benefit transaction history for one employee. |
| `createBenefitLog(payload)` | `benefit_logs` | Creates a manual benefit log entry. |
| `patchBenefitLog(id, payload)` | `benefit_logs` | Updates a benefit log entry. |
| `deleteBenefitLog(id)` | `benefit_logs` | Deletes a benefit log entry. |
| `fetchSalarySchedules()` | `salary_schedules` | Lists government DBM Salary Grade schedules (SG 1-33, Steps 1-8). |

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- user_wage_management: Active wage profile per employee
CREATE TABLE `user_wage_management` (
  `id`                              INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`                         INT NOT NULL,
  `daily_wage`                      DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `schedule_id`                     BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,       -- FK to salary_schedules (DBM grade)
  `cutoff_wage_date_update`         DATE NULL,
  `philhealth_contribution_monthly` DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `sss_contribution_monthly`        DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `pagibig_contribution_monthly`    DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `isCard`                          TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',     -- 1=paid via ATM card
  `isRegularEmployee`               TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `vacation_leave_per_year`         INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `sick_leave_per_year`             INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `paid_holiday`                    TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `created_date`                    DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `created_by`                      INT NULL,
  `updated_date`                    DATETIME NULL ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `updated_by`                      INT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_user_wage_schedule`
    FOREIGN KEY (`schedule_id`) REFERENCES `salary_schedules` (`schedule_id`)
    ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE SET NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- user_wage_history: Immutable audit trail of all wage changes
CREATE TABLE `user_wage_history` (
  `history_id`                      INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_wage_id`                    INT NOT NULL,                -- ID of the wage record changed
  `user_id`                         INT NOT NULL,
  `daily_wage`                      DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  `philhealth_contribution_monthly` DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `sss_contribution_monthly`        DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `pagibig_contribution_monthly`    DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `vacation_leave_per_year`         INT NOT NULL,
  `sick_leave_per_year`             INT NOT NULL,
  `paid_holiday`                    TINYINT(1) NOT NULL,
  `valid_from`                      DATETIME NOT NULL,
  `valid_to`                        DATETIME NULL,
  `change_type`                     ENUM('INSERT','UPDATE','DELETE') NOT NULL,
  `changed_by`                      INT NULL,
  `changed_at`                      DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  PRIMARY KEY (`history_id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- user_wage_proration_log: Records mid-cutoff salary changes for day-by-day proration
CREATE TABLE `user_wage_proration_log` (
  `id`                  INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`             INT NOT NULL,
  `previous_daily_wage` DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  `new_daily_wage`      DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  `effective_date`      DATE NOT NULL,              -- date the new rate takes effect
  `cutoff_id`           INT NOT NULL,               -- which cutoff period this change falls in
  `updated_by`          INT NOT NULL,
  `created_at`          DATETIME NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- user_wage_access_log: Security audit — every wage view or edit is logged
CREATE TABLE `user_wage_access_log` (
  `id`         INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`    INT NOT NULL,                        -- employee whose data was accessed
  `opened_by`  INT NOT NULL,                        -- HR user who opened it
  `opened_at`  DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `remarks`    VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- salary_schedules: Government DBM Salary Grade reference table
CREATE TABLE `salary_schedules` (
  `schedule_id`    BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `effectivity_date` DATE NOT NULL COMMENT 'DBM schedule effectivity date e.g. 2023-01-01',
  `salary_grade`   TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,       -- 1 to 33
  `step`           TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,        -- 1 to 8
  `monthly_rate`   DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  `created_at`     TIMESTAMP NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `updated_at`     TIMESTAMP NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`schedule_id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uniq_schedule` (`effectivity_date`, `salary_grade`, `step`) USING BTREE,
  CONSTRAINT `salary_schedules_chk_1` CHECK (`salary_grade` BETWEEN 1 AND 33),
  CONSTRAINT `salary_schedules_chk_2` CHECK (`step` BETWEEN 1 AND 8)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

---

### 4. REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS

**Scenario A — Salary Rate Update**

> Event 1: HR opens the Wage module and searches for "Juan dela Cruz." A password prompt appears.
> Event 2: HR enters the security password. `verifyPassword()` is called. On success, `logWageAccess()` records who opened the wage data.
> Event 3: HR changes the daily wage from ₱750 to ₱850 with effective date July 10. `patchWage()` updates `user_wage_management`. The system also calls `createWageProrationLog()` to log the rate change in `user_wage_proration_log` for proration in the next payroll run.

**Scenario B — Adding a Vale Loan**

> Event 1: HR selects the Loans tab for an employee and clicks "Add Loan."
> Event 2: HR enters loan type = VALE, amount = ₱3,000, 3 months to pay. `createEmployeeLoan()` writes to `employee_loan`.
> Event 3: During the next payroll run, `loadWorkspace()` picks up this active loan and deducts 50% of the monthly payment (₱500) per cutoff in `loan_vale` on `payroll_run_employee`.

---

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **Password verification is not optional.** `verifyPassword()` must succeed before wage data is displayed or modified. The UI enforces this gate.
- **Proration log drives the payroll engine.** If a wage change is saved without a corresponding `user_wage_proration_log` entry, the payroll engine will use the flat current rate for all days — the employee will NOT be prorated. Always create the proration log alongside wage updates.
- **DBM check constraints.** `salary_schedules` enforces `salary_grade` must be 1–33 and `step` must be 1–8 at the database level. Inserting invalid values will throw a constraint error.

# MODULE 3: Benefit Settings, Loans & Logs

**Path:** `modules/benefit-settings/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/benefit/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

This module manages the three statutory government benefit programmes: **SSS** (Social Security System), **PhilHealth** (National Health Insurance), and **Pag-IBIG** (Home Development Mutual Fund). It has three responsibilities:

1. **Cutoff Schedule Configuration** — Tells the payroll engine which cutoff (1st or 2nd) each benefit should be deducted on.
2. **Benefit Loan Management** — Tracks SSS and Pag-IBIG loan repayments (PhilHealth has no loan programme). Calculates amortization schedules and projects future deduction dates.
3. **Benefit Log Viewer** — Read-only audit trail showing every contribution and loan deduction that has been processed through payroll, sourced from both `payroll_run_employee` and the `benefit_logs` table.

---

### 2. FILES & FUNCTIONS

#### `providers/benefitApi.ts`

| Function | DB Collection | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fetchCompanyConfig()` | *(config endpoint)* | Fetches the company name from the API config. |
| `fullnameFromUser(u)` | *(utility)* | Helper to format an employee's full name from their user record. |
| `formatMoney(v)` | *(utility)* | Formats a number to 2 decimal places as a string. |
| `toNum(v)` | *(utility)* | Safely parses any value to a number, handling strings with commas. |
| `cutoffLabel(c)` | *(utility)* | Formats a cutoff period into a human-readable label e.g. "Jul 01, 2026 – Jul 15, 2026 (FIRST)". |
| `computeLoanCutoffSchedule(args)` | *(utility)* | Given a loan and the list of all cutoffs, projects which cutoffs the loan will be deducted on, returning: `all`, `paid`, `upcoming`, `nextDue`, `endDue`. |
| `isLoanDueOnCutoff(args)` | *(utility)* | Returns `true` if a specific loan is scheduled for deduction on a given cutoff period. |
| `buildLoanPayload(input)` | *(utility)* | Validates and builds the database payload for a benefit loan. Throws an error if someone tries to create a PhilHealth loan (which is not allowed). |
| `fetchBenefitSettings()` | `benefit_cutoff_settings` | Loads the current deduction schedule settings (which cutoff each benefit is deducted on). |
| `fetchUsers()` | `user` | Lists all employees (for the loan employee selector). |
| `fetchDepartments()` | `department` | Lists all departments. |
| `saveBenefitSetting(setting)` | `benefit_cutoff_settings` | Creates or updates the cutoff assignment for a benefit (POST if new, PATCH if updating). |
| `fetchCutoffSettings()` | `cutoff_settings` | Loads all cutoff periods — used to display the loan amortization schedule timeline. |
| `fetchBenefitLoans()` | `benefit_loans` | Lists all SSS and Pag-IBIG loans across all employees. |
| `createBenefitLoan(input)` | `benefit_loans` | Creates a new government loan record. |
| `updateBenefitLoan(loanId, input)` | `benefit_loans` | Updates an existing government loan. |
| `deleteBenefitLoan(loanId)` | `benefit_loans` | Deletes a government loan record. |
| `fetchBenefitLogs()` | `payroll_run_employee`, `benefit_logs` | Reads benefit deduction history from two sources: system-automated (from `payroll_run_employee`) and manual (from `benefit_logs`). |

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- benefit_cutoff_settings: Which payroll cutoff deducts each benefit
CREATE TABLE `benefit_cutoff_settings` (
  `id`             INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `benefit_code`   ENUM('SSS','PAGIBIG','PHILHEALTH') NOT NULL,
  `benefit_name`   VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  `cutoff`         ENUM('FIRST','SECOND') NOT NULL,  -- which cutoff deducts this benefit
  `is_active`      TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  `effective_from` DATE NULL,
  `effective_to`   DATE NULL,
  `created_by`     INT NULL,
  `created_date`   DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `updated_by`     INT NULL,
  `updated_date`   DATETIME NULL ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_benefit_code` (`benefit_code`) USING BTREE -- one row per benefit type
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- benefit_loans: Government statutory loan records (SSS and Pag-IBIG only)
CREATE TABLE `benefit_loans` (
  `loan_id`              BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`              INT NOT NULL,
  `benefit_code`         ENUM('SSS','PAGIBIG') NOT NULL,    -- PhilHealth NOT allowed here
  `loan_name`            VARCHAR(80) NULL,
  `reference_no`         VARCHAR(60) NULL,
  `principal_amount`     DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `interest_amount`      DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `total_payable`        DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `accumulated_amount`   DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `amortization_amount`  DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',  -- per installment amount
  `terms_installments`   INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',               -- total number of payments
  `deduct_on`            ENUM('FIRST','SECOND','BOTH') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'BOTH',
  `start_cutoff_id`      INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,                  -- cutoff when deductions begin
  `paid_installments`    INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `remaining_balance`    DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `last_paid_cutoff_id`  VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `status`               ENUM('ACTIVE','CLOSED','CANCELLED') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE',
  `remarks`              VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `created_by`           INT NULL,
  `created_date`         DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `updated_by`           INT NULL,
  `updated_date`         DATETIME NULL ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`loan_id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- benefit_logs: Immutable audit ledger for all benefit contributions and loan deductions
CREATE TABLE `benefit_logs` (
  `benefit_log_id`    BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `cutoff_id`         INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `cutoff_start`      DATE NULL,
  `cutoff_end`        DATE NULL,
  `cutoff_type`       ENUM('FIRST','SECOND') NULL,
  `user_id`           INT NOT NULL,
  `benefit_code`      ENUM('SSS','PAGIBIG','PHILHEALTH') NOT NULL,
  `log_type`          ENUM('CONTRIBUTION','LOAN') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'CONTRIBUTION',
  `loan_id`           BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,                -- required if log_type = LOAN
  `source_amount`     DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `deducted_amount`   DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `payroll_run_id`    BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `payroll_detail_id` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `note`              VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `created_date`      DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  PRIMARY KEY (`benefit_log_id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_blog_unique`
    (`cutoff_id`, `user_id`, `benefit_code`, `log_type`, `loan_id`, `payroll_run_id`) USING BTREE,
  -- Business rule: LOAN log_type requires loan_id; CONTRIBUTION must not have loan_id
  CONSTRAINT `chk_loan_id_required_for_loan`
    CHECK ((`log_type` = 'CONTRIBUTION' AND `loan_id` IS NULL)
        OR (`log_type` = 'LOAN' AND `loan_id` IS NOT NULL)),
  -- Business rule: PhilHealth cannot have loan log entries
  CONSTRAINT `chk_loan_not_philhealth`
    CHECK (`log_type` = 'CONTRIBUTION'
        OR (`log_type` = 'LOAN' AND `benefit_code` IN ('SSS','PAGIBIG')))
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

---

### 4. REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS

**Scenario A — Configuring Pag-IBIG to 2nd Cutoff**

> Event 1: HR opens Benefit Settings and changes Pag-IBIG from "FIRST" to "SECOND" cutoff.
> Event 2: `saveBenefitSetting()` calls `PATCH /items/benefit_cutoff_settings/{id}` with `cutoff = 'SECOND'`.
> Event 3: On the next payroll run, `loadWorkspace()` reads this updated setting. `computeEmployeeLine()` only deducts Pag-IBIG from employees in the SECOND cutoff run.

**Scenario B — SSS Salary Loan Entry**

> Event 1: HR enters a new SSS Salary Loan for an employee: principal ₱10,000, amortization ₱833.33/month, 12 installments, starting from Cutoff ID 45.
> Event 2: `createBenefitLoan()` writes to `benefit_loans` with `deduct_on = 'BOTH'` and `start_cutoff_id = 45`.
> Event 3: `computeLoanCutoffSchedule()` projects the next 24 cutoffs (12 months × 2 cutoffs), showing each scheduled deduction date. Per cutoff, ₱416.67 is deducted (50% of monthly amortization for BOTH mode).

---

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **PhilHealth has no loan type.** The `benefit_loans` table and all UI flows enforce `benefit_code IN ('SSS','PAGIBIG')` only. The `chk_loan_not_philhealth` constraint at the database level will reject any violation.
- **`uq_benefit_code` means one row per benefit.** There will only ever be 3 rows in `benefit_cutoff_settings` — one for SSS, one for PhilHealth, one for Pag-IBIG. `saveBenefitSetting()` always does a PATCH on the existing row.

---

# MODULE 4: Cutoff Settings & Period Management

**Path:** `modules/cutoff-settings/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/cutoff-settings/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

Defines the payroll calendar — the date ranges for each 1st and 2nd cutoff period. The module enforces that every payroll month always has exactly two defined periods (FIRST and SECOND), auto-creating them if they do not exist. All other modules reference cutoff records by their `id` to link payroll data to a specific period.

---

### 2. FILES & FUNCTIONS

#### `providers/cutoffSettingsApi.ts`

| Function | DB Collection | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `pad2(n)` | *(utility)* | Pads a single digit to two digits: `7` → `"07"`. |
| `ymd(year, month, day)` | *(utility)* | Builds a `YYYY-MM-DD` date string. |
| `computeCurrentPayrollPeriod(date)` | *(utility)* | Determines the payroll month for any given date. If today is the 26th or later, the payroll period is the *next* calendar month (since the 1st cutoff has already started for next month). |
| `prevMonth(period)` | *(utility)* | Returns the previous month's period key — used to calculate the FIRST cutoff start date. |
| `computeDefaultCutoffsForPeriod(period)` | *(utility)* | Calculates the default date ranges for a given payroll month: **FIRST** = previous month 26th to current month 10th; **SECOND** = current month 11th to 25th. |
| `getSessionUser()` | *(auth)* | Reads the logged-in user's JWT payload from the auth library. |
| `getSessionUserId()` | *(auth)* | Extracts the user ID from the logged-in session. |
| `formatUserFullName(u)` | *(utility)* | Builds a full name string from first, middle, and last name. |
| `makeUserNameMap(users)` | *(utility)* | Creates a Map from user IDs to display names — used to resolve "Updated By" names in the UI. |
| `listUsers(ids?)` | `user` | Fetches users from the API (for resolving "updated by" labels in the history table). |
| `getUserDisplayName(userNameMap, id)` | *(utility)* | Resolves a user ID to a name from the map, with fallback to the raw ID. |
| `listCutoffSettings(period)` | `cutoff_settings` | Fetches the two cutoff rows for a specific payroll month and year. |
| `listAllCutoffSettings()` | `cutoff_settings` | Fetches all cutoff rows across all months (used for loan schedule projections). |
| `upsertCutoffSettings(rows)` | `cutoff_settings`, `cutoff_settings_history` | Creates or updates cutoff date rows. On update, the history is automatically recorded via a DB trigger into `cutoff_settings_history`. |
| `ensureTwoRowsForCurrentPayrollPeriod(date?)` | `cutoff_settings` | **Critical initialisation function.** Checks if the current payroll month has both a FIRST and SECOND cutoff row. If either is missing, it automatically inserts the missing rows using default date calculations. This is called every time a user opens the Cutoff Settings page. |

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- cutoff_settings: Master calendar of payroll cutoff periods
CREATE TABLE `cutoff_settings` (
  `id`            BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `status`        VARCHAR(50) NULL DEFAULT 'published',
  `date_created`  TIMESTAMP NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `date_updated`  TIMESTAMP NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `month`         INT NOT NULL,                -- calendar month (1–12)
  `year`          INT NOT NULL,
  `cutoff_type`   VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,        -- 'FIRST' or 'SECOND'
  `start_date`    DATE NOT NULL,
  `end_date`      DATE NOT NULL,
  `payout_date`   DATE NULL,                   -- payday for this cutoff
  `period_status` VARCHAR(20) NULL DEFAULT 'OPEN',  -- 'OPEN' or 'CLOSED'
  `created_by`    VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `updated_by`    VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `unique_period_definition` (`month`, `year`, `cutoff_type`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- cutoff_settings_history: Full audit trail of every change to a cutoff period
CREATE TABLE `cutoff_settings_history` (
  `id`                  BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `cutoff_setting_id`   BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,   -- FK to cutoff_settings
  `event_type`          ENUM('INSERT','UPDATE','DELETE') NOT NULL,
  `event_at`            TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `changed_by`          VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `status`              VARCHAR(50) NULL DEFAULT 'published',
  `source_date_created` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  `source_date_updated` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  `month`               INT NOT NULL,
  `year`                INT NOT NULL,
  `cutoff_type`         VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  `start_date`          DATE NOT NULL,
  `end_date`            DATE NOT NULL,
  `payout_date`         DATE NULL,
  `period_status`       VARCHAR(20) NULL DEFAULT 'OPEN',
  `created_by`          VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `updated_by`          VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `raw_payload`         JSON NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_cutoff_settings_history_cutoff_setting_id`
    FOREIGN KEY (`cutoff_setting_id`) REFERENCES `cutoff_settings` (`id`)
    ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

---

### 4. REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS

**Scenario A — Auto-Initialisation on New Month**

> Event 1: It is August 1, 2026. HR opens the Cutoff Settings page.
> Event 2: `computeCurrentPayrollPeriod()` evaluates: day 1 < 26 → payroll month = August 2026.
> Event 3: `ensureTwoRowsForCurrentPayrollPeriod()` queries `cutoff_settings` for `month=8, year=2026`.
> Event 4: No rows found. `computeDefaultCutoffsForPeriod()` calculates: FIRST = July 26 – Aug 10, SECOND = Aug 11 – Aug 25.
> Event 5: Two rows are inserted into `cutoff_settings`. History is recorded in `cutoff_settings_history` with `event_type = 'INSERT'`.

---

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **Never delete a cutoff row that has payroll runs against it.** The `cutoff_settings_history` table has a RESTRICT foreign key — deletion will fail. Mark the period as `CLOSED` instead.
- **The `unique_period_definition` index** prevents duplicate FIRST/SECOND rows for the same month and year. Any attempt to insert a duplicate will fail with a database unique constraint error.

---

---

# MODULE 5: Calendar Management & Attendance

**Path:** `modules/calendar-management/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/calendar-management/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

Manages the company holiday calendar and provides a visual calendar interface for marking Regular, Special Non-Working, and Company-declared holidays. These holidays directly affect payroll computation: working on a declared holiday triggers higher pay multipliers in the Payroll Run Engine.

The module also serves as the system's view into raw biometric attendance records — displaying `attendance_log` data and showing which records are pending approval versus approved.

---

### 2. FILES & FUNCTIONS

#### `providers/calendarApi.ts`

| Function | DB Collection | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fetchHolidays()` | `holiday_calendar` | Loads all holiday records for display on the calendar grid. |
| `fetchUsers()` | `user` | Loads all users — used for linking attendance records to employee names. |
| `createHoliday(data)` | `holiday_calendar` | Creates a new holiday entry (Regular, Special, or Company). |
| `updateHoliday(id, data)` | `holiday_calendar` | Updates an existing holiday (change type, description, is_paid flag, etc.). |
| `deleteHoliday(id)` | `holiday_calendar` | Removes a holiday from the calendar. |

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- holiday_calendar: Master list of all holidays that affect payroll multipliers
CREATE TABLE `holiday_calendar` (
  `id`                  INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `holiday_date`        DATE NOT NULL,
  `cutoff_setting_id`   BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,           -- optional: link to a specific cutoff
  `last_working_day`    DATE NULL,                       -- if holiday shifts workday
  `description`         VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `holiday_type`        ENUM('regular','special','company') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'regular',
  `is_recurring`        TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1', -- 1 = annual recurring
  `is_paid`             TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1', -- 1 = employee gets paid if absent
  `created_by`          INT NULL,
  `created_date`        DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `updated_by`          INT NULL,
  `updated_date`        DATETIME NULL ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_holiday_date_type` (`holiday_date`, `holiday_type`) USING BTREE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_holiday_calendar_cutoff_setting`
    FOREIGN KEY (`cutoff_setting_id`) REFERENCES `cutoff_settings` (`id`)
    ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON DELETE NO ACTION
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- department_schedule: Standard work schedule per department
CREATE TABLE `department_schedule` (
  `schedule_id`   BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `department_id` INT NOT NULL,
  `working_days`  TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,           -- number of days per week
  `work_start`    TIME NOT NULL,
  `work_end`      TIME NOT NULL,
  `lunch_start`   TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '12:00:00',
  `lunch_end`     TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '13:00:00',
  `break_start`   TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '15:00:00',
  `break_end`     TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '15:30:00',
  `workdays_note` VARCHAR(64) NULL,
  `grace_period`  TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT '5', -- minutes before marking Late
  `created_at`    DATETIME NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `updated_at`    DATETIME NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`schedule_id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_department_schedule` (`department_id`) USING BTREE, -- one schedule per dept
  CONSTRAINT `FK_department_schedule_department`
    FOREIGN KEY (`department_id`) REFERENCES `department` (`department_id`)
    ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON DELETE NO ACTION
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- attendance_log: Raw biometric clock-in / clock-out records
CREATE TABLE `attendance_log` (
  `log_id`          BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`         INT NOT NULL,
  `department_id`   INT NOT NULL,
  `log_date`        DATE NOT NULL,
  `time_in`         DATETIME NULL,
  `lunch_start`     DATETIME NULL,
  `lunch_end`       DATETIME NULL,
  `break_start`     DATETIME NULL,
  `break_end`       DATETIME NULL,
  `time_out`        DATETIME NULL,
  `image_time_in`   VARCHAR(255) NULL,                 -- face image file path
  `image_time_out`  VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `status`          ENUM('On Time','Late','Absent','Half Day','Incomplete','Leave','Holiday')
                    NULL DEFAULT 'On Time',
  `created_at`      TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `updated_at`      TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `approval_status` ENUM('pending','approved','rejected') NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  PRIMARY KEY (`log_id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_user_date` (`user_id`, `log_date`) USING BTREE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_att_user`
    FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON DELETE NO ACTION
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- attendance_approval: Supervisor-approved summarised attendance — this is what payroll uses
CREATE TABLE `attendance_approval` (
  `approval_id`         BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `employee_id`         BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `date_schedule`       DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '1970-01-01',
  `approved_by`         INT NOT NULL,
  `approved_at`         DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `work_minutes`        INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',       -- total minutes worked
  `late_minutes`        INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `undertime_minutes`   INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `overtime_minutes`    INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `remarks`             VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `status`              ENUM('approved','rejected') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'approved',
  PRIMARY KEY (`approval_id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

---

### 4. REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS

**Scenario A — Declaring Independence Day as a Paid Regular Holiday**

> Event 1: HR opens the calendar and clicks on June 12.
> Event 2: HR sets `holiday_type = 'regular'`, `is_paid = 1`, `description = 'Independence Day'`. `createHoliday()` writes to `holiday_calendar`.
> Event 3: On the next payroll run, `loadWorkspace()` fetches this entry. Any employee with approved attendance on June 12 will receive a 2.0× base pay multiplier. Employees who were absent still receive paid holiday pay since `is_paid = 1`.

---

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **Only `attendance_approval` drives payroll.** The payroll engine ignores `attendance_log` entirely. Only supervisor-approved records from `attendance_approval` are used for pay calculations.
- **Unique constraint on `(holiday_date, holiday_type)`.** The same date cannot have two holiday entries of the same type. However, a date can have both a `regular` and a `company` holiday entry, which the payroll engine will combine using the highest multiplier.

---

---

# MODULE 6: Coop Management & Employee Loans

**Path:** `modules/coop-management/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/coop/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

Manages the company's internal cooperative savings programme and employee loans. It tracks who is a coop savings member, how much they contribute monthly, and the full history of those contributions. It also handles employee loans (Vale, Car Loan, Coop-type loans) — separate from government statutory loans.

The module uses a single generic API client (`coopApi.ts`) that routes requests to any of its supported collections.

---

### 2. FILES & FUNCTIONS

#### `providers/coopApi.ts`

| Function | DB Collection | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `listItems(collection, params, signal)` | Varies | Generic paginated list fetcher. Accepts `employee_loan`, `user`, `employee_loan_payment`, `coop_savings_membership`, or `cutoff_settings`. |
| `createItem(collection, body)` | Varies | Generic item creator — POSTs to the specified collection. |
| `updateItem(collection, id, body)` | Varies | Generic item updater — PATCHes the specified item by ID. |
| `deleteItem(collection, id)` | Varies | Generic item deleter — sends DELETE to the specified collection. |

The `CoopCollection` type limits which collections this API client can access:  
`"employee_loan" | "user" | "employee_loan_payment" | "coop_savings_membership" | "cutoff_settings"`

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- coop_savings_membership: Employee cooperative savings membership record
CREATE TABLE `coop_savings_membership` (
  `id`                  BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`             INT NOT NULL,
  `membership_id`       VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,                -- coop membership card number
  `monthly_amount`      DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,              -- monthly savings target
  `total_collection`    DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `total_months`        INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `start_date`          DATE NOT NULL,
  `end_date`            DATE NULL,
  `is_active`           TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  `created_by`          INT NULL,
  `created_date`        DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `last_paid_cutoff_id` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `updated_by`          INT NULL,
  `updated_date`        DATETIME NULL ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- coop_savings_contribution: Log of savings contributions posted per payroll period
CREATE TABLE `coop_savings_contribution` (
  `id`            BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `membership_id` BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `user_id`       INT NOT NULL,
  `period_month`  DATE NOT NULL,                 -- first day of the month this covers
  `amount`        DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  `reference_no`  VARCHAR(100) NULL,
  `remarks`       VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `posted_by`     INT NULL,
  `posted_at`     DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- employee_loan: Internal company loans (Vale, Car Loan, Coop-type)
CREATE TABLE `employee_loan` (
  `loan_id`               BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`               INT NOT NULL,
  `loan_type`             ENUM('VALE','CAR LOAN','COOP') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'COOP',
  `loan_amount`           DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  `interest_rate`         DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '3.00',
  `interest_amount`       DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  `net_amount_released`   DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  `accumulated_amount`    DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,   -- total paid so far
  `months_to_pay`         INT NOT NULL,
  `monthly_payment`       DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  `start_date`            DATE NOT NULL,
  `end_date`              DATE NULL,
  `status`                ENUM('ACTIVE','PAID','CANCELLED') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE',
  `last_paid_cutoff_id`   VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `created_by`            INT NULL,
  `created_date`          DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `updated_by`            INT NULL,
  `updated_date`          DATETIME NULL ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`loan_id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- employee_loan_payment: Individual payments posted against employee loans
CREATE TABLE `employee_loan_payment` (
  `payment_id`    BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `loan_id`       BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `user_id`       INT NOT NULL,
  `payment_date`  DATE NOT NULL,
  `period_month`  DATE NOT NULL,
  `amount_paid`   DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  `reference_no`  VARCHAR(100) NULL,
  `remarks`       VARCHAR(255) NULL,

) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

---

### 4. REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS

**Scenario A — Coop Savings Monthly Deduction**

> Event 1: An employee's `coop_savings_membership` record shows `monthly_amount = 500.00`.
> Event 2: During payroll computation, `loadWorkspace()` fetches this active membership.
> Event 3: `computeEmployeeLine()` deducts ₱250.00 from each cutoff (₱500 ÷ 2) as `coop_savings` on `payroll_run_employee`.

---

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **`listItems()`, `createItem()`, `updateItem()`, `deleteItem()` are generic.** The collection name is passed as a parameter. Always use only collections listed in the `CoopCollection` type to avoid unauthorised access.

# MODULE 7: Allowance Management

**Path:** `modules/allowance/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/allowance/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

Manages recurring and one-time employee allowances (e.g. Meal Allowance, Transportation Allowance). Recurring allowances can be set to pay `PER_CUTOFF` (full amount each cutoff) or `PER_MONTH` (split 50/50 between the two cutoffs). One-time allowances are applied only once during a specific cutoff window and then marked as processed.

---

### 2. FILES & FUNCTIONS

#### `providers/allowanceApi.ts`

| Function | DB Collection | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `iso(date)` | *(utility)* | Formats a JavaScript Date to `YYYY-MM-DD` string. |
| `formatCurrency(v)` | *(utility)* | Formats a number to Philippine Peso currency display. |
| `fullnameFromUser(u)` | *(utility)* | Builds full name from user fields. |
| `flagToBool(v)` | *(utility)* | Converts a Directus bit/buffer/0/1 value to a JavaScript boolean. |
| `computeCutoffFromDate(dStr)` | *(utility)* | Given any date, calculates the cutoff window it falls in (11–25 = 2nd cutoff; 26–10 across months = 1st cutoff). |
| `getAllowancesList(params)` | `employee_allowance` | Fetches paginated allowances with filters for mode (recurring/one-time), status (active/inactive, processed/unprocessed), pay cycle, description search, and specific employee IDs. |
| `createAllowance(payload)` | `employee_allowance` | Creates a new allowance record (recurring or one-time). |
| `updateAllowance(id, payload)` | `employee_allowance` | Updates an existing allowance. |
| `deleteAllowance(id)` | `employee_allowance` | Deletes an allowance record. |
| `useAllowances(params)` | `employee_allowance` | SWR React hook that reactively fetches allowances with automatic caching. |

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- employee_allowance: Recurring and one-time allowance definitions per employee
CREATE TABLE `employee_allowance` (
  `allowance_id`  BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`       INT NOT NULL,
  `amount`        DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  `description`   VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `cutoff_start`  DATE NULL,                    -- for one-time: target cutoff start
  `cutoff_end`    DATE NULL,                    -- for one-time: target cutoff end
  `is_recurring`  TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',  -- 0=one-time, 1=recurring
  `is_active`     TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',  -- for recurring: active/inactive
  `pay_cycle`     ENUM('N/A','PER_CUTOFF','PER_MONTH') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'N/A',
  `start_date`    DATE NULL,                    -- for recurring: effective start
  `end_date`      DATE NULL,                    -- for recurring: effective end (null = indefinite)
  `is_processed`  TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',  -- for one-time: 1 after payroll processes it
  `created_by`    INT NULL,
  `created_date`  DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `updated_by`    INT NULL,
  `updated_date`  DATETIME NULL ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`allowance_id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

---

### 4. REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS

**Scenario A — PER_MONTH Recurring Meal Allowance**

> Event 1: HR creates a recurring meal allowance for an employee: amount = ₱2,000, pay_cycle = `PER_MONTH`.
> Event 2: During 1st Cutoff payroll, `computeEmployeeLine()` detects this recurring allowance with `PER_MONTH` cycle. It applies ₱1,000 (50% of ₱2,000).
> Event 3: During 2nd Cutoff payroll, the same ₱1,000 is applied again. The employee receives the full ₱2,000 across both cutoffs that month.

---

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **One-time allowances must be matched to a specific cutoff window** via `cutoff_start` and `cutoff_end`. The payroll engine will only include them if the active cutoff falls within that window. Once processed, `is_processed` is set to 1 and the allowance is skipped in future runs.

---

---

# MODULE 8: Additions & Deductions

**Path:** `modules/additions-deductions/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/additions-deductions/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

Provides a standalone CRUD interface for ad-hoc manual additions and manual/shortage deductions. Unlike the Allowance module (which manages structured recurring data), this module handles one-off, flat-amount adjustments that are applied to a specific cutoff period.

---

### 2. FILES & FUNCTIONS

#### `providers/additionsDeductionsApi.ts`

| Function | DB Collection | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `getUsers()` | `user` | Fetches all users for the employee selector. |
| `getAdditions()` | `payroll_other_additions` | Fetches all manual addition records. |
| `getDeductions()` | `payroll_other_deductions` | Fetches all manual deduction records. |
| `createRecord(resource, data)` | `payroll_other_additions` or `payroll_other_deductions` | Creates a new addition or deduction depending on `resource` parameter. |
| `updateRecord(resource, id, data)` | `payroll_other_additions` or `payroll_other_deductions` | Updates an existing record. |
| `deleteRecord(resource, id)` | `payroll_other_additions` or `payroll_other_deductions` | Deletes an additions or deductions record. |

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- payroll_other_additions: Manual one-off earnings additions for a specific cutoff
CREATE TABLE `payroll_other_additions` (
  `id`           INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`      INT NOT NULL,
  `amount`       DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `description`  VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `cutoff_start` DATE NOT NULL,               -- start of the target cutoff window
  `cutoff_end`   DATE NOT NULL,               -- end of the target cutoff window
  `created_by`   INT NULL,
  `created_date` DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- payroll_other_deductions: Manual deductions (shortage cash overs or miscellaneous)
CREATE TABLE `payroll_other_deductions` (
  `id`           INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`      INT NOT NULL,
  `amount`       DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `type`         ENUM('SHORTAGE','MANUAL') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'MANUAL',
  `description`  VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `cutoff_start` DATE NOT NULL,
  `cutoff_end`   DATE NOT NULL,
  `created_by`   INT NULL,
  `created_date` DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- dr_payment: Delivery receipt payment deductions (for logistics store shortages)
CREATE TABLE `dr_payment` (
  `dr_payment_id`           INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `delivery_receipt_number` VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `employee_id`             INT NOT NULL,
  `cutoff_from`             DATE NOT NULL,
  `cutoff_to`               DATE NOT NULL,
  `payroll_ref_no`          VARCHAR(50) NULL,
  `is_posted_to_payroll`    TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',  -- 0=pending, 1=already deducted
  `payment_date`            DATE NOT NULL,
  `amount_paid`             DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0.00',
  `payment_method`          ENUM('PAYROLL_DEDUCTION','CASH','CHECK','BANK_TRANSFER','OTHERS')
                            NULL DEFAULT 'PAYROLL_DEDUCTION',
  `remarks`                 VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `created_at`              DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `created_by`              INT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`dr_payment_id`) USING BTREE,
  INDEX `idx_dr_payment_employee` (`employee_id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

---

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **DR payments with `payment_method = 'PAYROLL_DEDUCTION'` and `is_posted_to_payroll = 0`** are automatically pulled by the payroll engine during `loadWorkspace()`. Once payroll is posted, `payroll_source_posting` records the deduction and `dr_payment.is_posted_to_payroll` is set to 1.
- **Shortage vs Manual.** Use `type = 'SHORTAGE'` for cash shortage accountability deductions. Use `type = 'MANUAL'` for any other deduction type. This distinction flows through to the payroll breakdown display.

---

# MODULE 9: Retroactive Pay

**Path:** `modules/retro/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/retro/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

Handles back-pay adjustments — cases where an employee's salary increase or correction was approved after the cutoff period it should have applied to. HR creates a retro pay record specifying the employee, the amount, and the cutoff window it targets. During the next payroll run for that cutoff period, the amount is picked up and added to `retro_pay` on the employee's payroll line.

---

### 2. FILES & FUNCTIONS

#### `providers/retroApi.ts`

All functions are methods of the exported `retroApi` object:

| Method | DB Collection | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `retroApi.fetchAll()` | `retro_pay` | Fetches all retro pay records across all employees. |
| `retroApi.create(data, createdBy)` | `retro_pay` | Creates a new retro pay entry. Parses `user_id`, `amount`, `cutoff_start`, `cutoff_end`, and `description` from the form state. |
| `retroApi.update(id, data, updatedBy)` | `retro_pay` | Updates an existing retro pay record. |
| `retroApi.delete(id)` | `retro_pay` | Deletes a retro pay entry. |

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- retro_pay: Retroactive pay adjustments to be applied in a specific cutoff window
CREATE TABLE `retro_pay` (
  `retro_id`     BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id`      INT NOT NULL,
  `amount`       DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  `description`  VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `cutoff_start` DATE NOT NULL,                -- target cutoff window start
  `cutoff_end`   DATE NOT NULL,                -- target cutoff window end
  `is_processed` TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',  -- 0=pending, 1=included in payroll
  `created_by`   INT NULL,
  `created_date` DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `updated_by`   INT NULL,
  `updated_date` DATETIME NULL ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`retro_id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

---

### 4. REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS

**Scenario A — Retroactive Pay from a Missed Salary Increase**

> Event 1: An employee's salary was increased in June but the HR admin forgot to update the payroll. In July, HR realises the June payroll shortfall was ₱1,500.
> Event 2: HR opens Retro Pay and creates a record: `user_id = 42`, `amount = 1500`, `cutoff_start = 2026-07-01`, `cutoff_end = 2026-07-15`.
> Event 3: During the July 1st Cutoff payroll run, `loadWorkspace()` fetches this record (`is_processed = 0`, dates match).
> Event 4: `computeEmployeeLine()` adds ₱1,500 to `retro_pay` on the employee's payroll line. After payroll posting, `is_processed` is set to 1.

---

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **Retro pay uses strict cutoff containment.** The payroll engine requires `retro_start >= cutoff_start` AND `retro_end <= cutoff_end`. A retro record that spans across two cutoffs will NOT be picked up by either. The dates must match exactly.
- **`is_processed = 1` is a locking flag.** Once the payroll posts, this flag prevents the amount from being deducted twice in a future run.

---

---

# MODULE 10: Payroll Records & Top Sheet

**Path:** `modules/payroll-records/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/payroll-records/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

The historical archive and reporting portal. Allows HR and management to view past posted payrolls, generate department-level Top Sheet summaries (showing gross pay, all deduction categories, and net pay per employee), and trigger payslip PDF generation. All data is read-only — this module does not modify any records.

---

### 2. FILES & FUNCTIONS

#### `providers/payrollRecordsApi.ts`

| Function | DB Collection | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fetchEmployees()` | `user` | Fetches the employee list for the filter selectors. |
| `fetchDepartments()` | `department` | Fetches all departments for the department filter. |
| `fetchCutoffs()` | `cutoff_settings` | Fetches all cutoff periods for the cutoff period selector. |
| `fetchTapSheet(args)` | `payroll_run_employee` | **Main reporting function.** Fetches all employee payroll lines for a given cutoff date range and department name, returning the full computed register for the Top Sheet report. |

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

> This module reads from `payroll_run`, `payroll_run_employee`, `payroll_payslip`, `department`, `user`, and `cutoff_settings`. All DDLs for these tables are documented under **Module 1** (Payroll Run Engine) and **Module 11** (Authentication & Organization).

---

### 4. REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS

**Scenario A — Generating a July Top Sheet**

> Event 1: Manager selects July 2026 1st Cutoff and "All Departments" in Payroll Records.
> Event 2: `fetchTapSheet()` queries `payroll_run_employee` filtered by `cutoff_start = 2026-07-01` and `cutoff_end = 2026-07-15`, joined to the POSTED `payroll_run`.
> Event 3: The Top Sheet renders each employee row with: Name, Basic Pay, OT, Holiday Pay, Allowances, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, Loans, Net Pay, and column subtotals.

---

# MODULE 11: Authentication, User & Organizational Master Data

**Path:** `modules/auth/`, `modules/profile/`, `modules/settings/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/auth/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

The foundational data layer. Manages user accounts, login credentials, session tokens, department hierarchies, employee profiles (government IDs, biometric IDs, emergency contacts), bank reference data, and on-call supervisor shift schedules. All other modules reference `user.user_id` and `department.department_id` as their core foreign keys.

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- user: Master employee/user record
CREATE TABLE `user` (
  `user_id`                   INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_email`                VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `user_password`             VARCHAR(255) NULL,                -- hashed (legacy)
  `user_fname`                VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `user_mname`                VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `user_lname`                VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `user_contact`              VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `user_province`             VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `user_city`                 VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `user_brgy`                 VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `user_department`           INT NULL,                         -- FK to department.department_id
  `user_sss`                  VARCHAR(255) NULL,                -- SSS ID number
  `user_philhealth`           VARCHAR(255) NULL,                -- PhilHealth ID
  `user_tin`                  VARCHAR(255) NULL,                -- Tax Identification Number
  `user_position`             VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `user_dateOfHire`           DATE NOT NULL,
  `user_tags`                 VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `user_bday`                 DATE NULL,
  `role_id`                   INT NULL,
  `user_image`                TEXT NULL,
  `biometric_id`              VARCHAR(255) NULL,                -- for biometric clock-in
  `rf_id`                     VARCHAR(255) NULL,                -- RFID card number
  `isAdmin`                   TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `user_pagibig`              VARCHAR(255) NULL,                -- Pag-IBIG ID
  `signature`                 TEXT NULL,
  `emergency_contact_name`    VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `emergency_contact_number`  VARCHAR(50) NULL,
  `role`                      VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USER',
  `hash_password`             VARCHAR(255) NULL,                -- bcrypt hash (current)
  `is_deleted`                BIT(1) NULL,                      -- soft delete flag
  PRIMARY KEY (`user_id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- department: Organisational unit definitions
CREATE TABLE `department` (
  `department_id`          INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `department_name`        VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `parent_division`        INT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `department_description` TEXT NULL,
  `department_head`        VARCHAR(255) NULL,                    -- name string (legacy)
  `department_head_id`     INT NULL,                             -- FK to user.user_id
  `tax_id`                 INT NULL,
  `date_added`             DATE NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`department_id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `department_name` (`department_name`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- bank_names: Reference list of banks for direct deposit setup
CREATE TABLE `bank_names` (
  `id`        INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `bank_name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- oncall_list: Employees assigned to an on-call schedule group
CREATE TABLE `oncall_list` (
  `id`            BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `dept_sched_id` BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,                     -- FK to oncall_schedule
  `user_id`       INT NOT NULL,                                  -- FK to user
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_oncalllist_user`
    FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`)
    ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- oncall_schedule: Shift schedule definitions for on-call personnel groups
CREATE TABLE `oncall_schedule` (
  `id`            BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `department_id` INT NOT NULL,
  `group`         VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  `working_days`  INT NOT NULL,
  `work_start`    TIME NOT NULL,
  `work_end`      TIME NOT NULL,
  `lunch_start`   TIME NULL DEFAULT '12:00:00',
  `lunch_end`     TIME NULL DEFAULT '13:00:00',
  `break_start`   TIME NULL DEFAULT '15:00:00',
  `break_end`     TIME NULL DEFAULT '15:30:00',
  `workdays`      VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  `grace_period`  TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT '5',
  `created_at`    DATETIME NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
  `updated_at`    DATETIME NULL,
  `encoder_id`    INT NOT NULL,
  `schedule_date` DATE NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_oncallsched_department`
    FOREIGN KEY (`department_id`) REFERENCES `department` (`department_id`)
    ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

---

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **`is_deleted` is a soft-delete flag.** Employees are never physically deleted. The payroll engine filters out employees with `is_deleted = 1` via `isActiveByDeletedFlags()`.
- **`hash_password` vs `user_password`.** Two password columns exist. `hash_password` is the active bcrypt column. `user_password` is a legacy field. Always write to `hash_password` and authenticate against it.

# MODULE 12: Logistics Payroll Run Engine

**Path:** `modules/logistics-payroll-run/`  
**API Route:** `app/api/logistics-payroll-run/`

---

### 1. MODULE OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURE

> ⚠️ **Status: SCAFFOLDED — NOT YET IMPLEMENTED**

This module is designed to calculate payroll for logistics drivers and helpers based on trips completed, delivery areas, and vehicle classifications — rather than standard time-based payroll. All module files (`LogisticsPayrollRunModule.tsx`, `types.ts`, `index.ts`) are currently empty. The API route returns a placeholder JSON response only.

The full data model and intended workflow are designed and documented. The salary matrix lookup works as:

```
Dispatch Trip → Staff Role + Vehicle Type + Delivery Area → payroll_logistics_salary_matrix → wage_amount
```

---

### 3. DATABASE TABLES & DDLS

```sql
-- payroll_logistics_vehicle_type: Vehicle category classifications
CREATE TABLE `payroll_logistics_vehicle_type` (
  `id`              BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `vehicle_type_id` BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `vehicle_type`    ENUM('BELOW 10 WHEELER','10 WHEELER','TRAILER','N/A') NOT NULL,
  `created_by`      BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,
  `created_at`      DATETIME(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_vt_id` (`vehicle_type_id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_vt_name` (`vehicle_type`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- payroll_logistics_staff: Logistics driver and helper profiles with role and vehicle assignment
CREATE TABLE `payroll_logistics_staff` (
  `id`              BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `staff_id`        BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `role`            ENUM('Driver','Helper') NOT NULL,
  `employment_type` ENUM('EXTRA','PROBATIONARY','REGULAR(<10W)','REGULAR(10W/T)') NULL,
  `vehicle_type_id` BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,                    -- default vehicle for this staff
  `is_deleted`      TINYINT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `created_by`      BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,
  `created_at`      DATETIME(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_staff_id` (`staff_id`) USING BTREE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_staff_vehicle`
    FOREIGN KEY (`vehicle_type_id`) REFERENCES `payroll_logistics_vehicle_type` (`vehicle_type_id`)
    ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- payroll_logistics_area: Delivery zone definitions
CREATE TABLE `payroll_logistics_area` (
  `id`         BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `area_id`    BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `area_name`  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
  `max_days`   SMALLINT UNSIGNED NULL,
  `mode_type`  ENUM('DELIVERY','PICKUP ONLY','PICKUP W/ MP DELIVERY') NULL,
  `is_deleted` TINYINT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `created_by` BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,
  `created_at` DATETIME(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_area_id` (`area_id`) USING BTREE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- payroll_logistics_location: Customer delivery locations mapped to a delivery area
CREATE TABLE `payroll_logistics_location` (
  `id`          BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `location_id` BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `area_id`     BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `location`    VARCHAR(220) NOT NULL,
  `distance`    INT UNSIGNED NULL,
  `is_deleted`  TINYINT NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `created_by`  BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,
  `created_at`  DATETIME(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_location_id` (`location_id`) USING BTREE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_loc_area`
    FOREIGN KEY (`area_id`) REFERENCES `payroll_logistics_area` (`area_id`)
    ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```sql
-- payroll_logistics_salary_matrix: Wage rate per area + staff role + vehicle type combination
CREATE TABLE `payroll_logistics_salary_matrix` (
  `id`              BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `area_id`         BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `staff_id`        BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `vehicle_type_id` BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `wage_amount`     DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,               -- amount paid per qualifying trip
  `created_by`      BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,
  `created_at`      DATETIME(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)),
  `updated_by`      BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,
  `updated_at`      DATETIME(3) NULL ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) USING BTREE,
  UNIQUE INDEX `uq_salary_matrix_unique` (`area_id`, `staff_id`, `vehicle_type_id`) USING BTREE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_mat_area`
    FOREIGN KEY (`area_id`) REFERENCES `payroll_logistics_area` (`area_id`)
    ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_mat_staff`
    FOREIGN KEY (`staff_id`) REFERENCES `payroll_logistics_staff` (`staff_id`)
    ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_mat_vehicle`
    FOREIGN KEY (`vehicle_type_id`) REFERENCES `payroll_logistics_vehicle_type` (`vehicle_type_id`)
    ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

### 5. SYSTEM RULES & HANDOVER NOTES

- **This module must be built.** All source files are empty stubs. Priority: implement `LogisticsPayrollRunModule.tsx`, `types.ts`, and the providers referencing the data model above.
- **Unique triplet constraint on salary matrix.** Each combination of `(area_id, staff_id, vehicle_type_id)` can only have one wage rate. Attempting to insert a duplicate will fail.
